summary: Three fail-closed branches of --range-base have no test. The CLI test only covers a nonexistent sha (rev-parse fails), a tracked edit and a 151-line range. Nothing covers a real commit that is not an ancestor of HEAD (line 115), an untracked-only file (the collected.untracked half of line 116), or a classifier error in the range (line 119). If any of these regressed, a stale or unreadable range could plan a scoped pass instead of the full pass.
fix: In test/review-plan-cli.test.ts add three cases, each asserting FIX_RANGE: unread and NEXT: full: a range base on a side branch, a new untracked file after the fix commit, and a range that makes classifyDiff report an error.

summary: The new mapping of 'scoped' to 'full' in newShip never runs in any test. The simulated history never sets rangeRuntimeLines, so nextStep never returns 'scoped' and test/review-dispatch-compare.test.ts still only exercises full passes. The comparison script therefore reports no change for the scoped pass, and a wrong fullPasses count after a scoped pass would go unnoticed.
fix: Pass rangeRuntimeLines through the scenario outcomes (or set it from the fixture's fix size). Then add a review-dispatch-compare test asserting that a fixed-blocker scenario plans the scoped dispatch set and counts it as one full pass.

summary: In the scoped branch, the note that the specialist army was skipped is the else arm of the <reader> chain. When Step 11 is still pending or published numbers changed, the <reader> is added and no SKIP line records the skipped specialists. That breaks the bin header's 'one SKIP: per reviewer left out' contract for exactly the #19 shape (adversarialRan=false).
fix: Always push a 'specialists (scoped pass)' skip, and push the <reader> skip only in the final else.

summary: raisedBy() with its RAISERS list and one-entry RAISER_ALIASES map stamps raised_by on every classified finding 'for attributing passes later', but no code reads it: summarizeReviewLoop, the receipt and the queue ignore it, and the only consumers are tests and Step 9 prose that copies it into review-log rows
fix: drop raisedBy, RAISERS, RAISER_ALIASES and the raised_by stamp (and its Step 9 copy instruction) until a reader of the field exists; findings already carry the specialist tag

summary: The scoped-pass eligibility is checked once, at the decision after pass 1, and never checked again. bin/gstack-review-plan:111-120 counts PASS_HEAD..HEAD, the whole-diff depth and --touched-gate at that moment. Then decision 3 inserts Step 5 (pregate fail means fix and rerun), Steps 6-8 and the 'cut that growth' edits before pass 2. Pass 2 reuses the plan that picked it (line 16: 'a repeat uses the plan run that picked it') but reads `git diff $RANGE_BASE`, which by then includes those later edits, committed or not. A test-fix edit made in Step 5 can push the range past 150 runtime lines, touch an item-2.5 gate path, or raise the whole diff to full depth. Pass 2 still runs only the fix-check (its fix list names only the pass-1 fixes), the <reader> and the adversarial pass, never the specialist army. A full pass 2 goes stale the same way, but it fails safe. The scoped pass exists only because of a size and gate precondition, and nothing enforces that precondition at review time.
fix: At pass-2 entry, after Steps 5-8, run `gstack-review-plan --range-base $RANGE_BASE` again with the same history flags. Downgrade to the full pass unless it still prints NEXT: scoped. Or record the HEAD the scoped plan counted (FIX_RANGE head=) and require HEAD to equal it with a clean tree before dispatching a scoped set.
evidence: Coverage note: only non-fixture source was read in full (bin/gstack-review-plan, lib/review-depth.ts, lib/review-scope.ts, scripts/review-dispatch-compare.ts, ship/sections/<reader>.md.tmpl, docs, CHANGELOG). Test and fixture files were reviewed in SUMMARY mode only, from --stat. Those are test/review-depth.test.ts +100, review-plan-cli +42, review-scope +16, ship-receipt-depth +16 and size-ledger gsta152-pr-b.json +4, covering scoped planning, the CLI --range-base paths, raised_by stamping and receipt binding. Their payload bytes were not analyzed.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The fix range's own class is computed and then thrown away. bin/gstack-review-plan:118 runs classifyDiff on RANGE_BASE..HEAD but keeps only `errors` and `runtimeLines`; `range.class` and `range.reasons` are discarded. The only gate signal nextStep sees for the range is the agent-supplied `--touched-gate` flag (lib/review-depth.ts:226). The whole-diff classification does not cover everything the range classification catches. The case that slips through: a fix commit deletes a code or test file that the branch itself added earlier. Against the merge base, that file is net-absent, so the whole diff shows nothing. The range classifier raises it to `gate` ("deletes N code or test path(s)"), but that result is ignored. Test-only or deletion-only fixes also count 0 runtime lines, so the native adversarial pass is skipped too, and pass 2 runs only a fix-check and the <reader>. Under the old full pass 2, the testing specialist would have read it. Fix: keep the full pass when `range.class === 'gate'`, either by setting touchedGate from it or by mapping it to `unread`. Then derive touchedGate from the range instead of trusting the flag.

label: FIXABLE
summary: An empty or wrongly anchored range still plans a scoped pass. When `--range-base` resolves to HEAD, the ancestor check passes and collectCommit returns an empty diff, so runtime_lines=0. That happens if PASS_HEAD was captured after the fix commit, or if a later step re-saved it. nextStep then returns `scoped` even though `--fixed-blocking` says fixes landed. Reproduced at this head: `nextStep({last:'full',fullPasses:1,fixedBlocking:true,rangeRuntimeLines:0},'light')` returns `scoped`, and planReview dispatches only `["fix-check","<reader>"]`, skipping the native adversarial pass, specialists and <reader>. Every reviewer gets `git diff <RANGE_BASE>`, which is empty, so the blocking fix goes unreviewed while the pass still counts as full pass 2. A base captured partway through the fixes undercounts the same way. Fix: treat an empty range (resolved == HEAD, or no paths) as `unread` whenever fixedBlocking is set. Better still, take the base from the previous pass's logged `commit_full`, as fixRangeBase in lib/review-evidence.ts already does for `--fix-range`, instead of from an agent shell variable.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The plan goes stale before pass 2 runs (time-of-check/time-of-use). The decision reads FIX_RANGE and the depth at the end of pass N. Decision 3 then inserts Step 5 and Steps 6–8 before Step 9 ("Tests must pass", plus "cut that growth"). The template also says "a repeat uses the plan run that picked it" (<reader>.md.tmpl:16). So test-repair edits and other changes committed after the decision are reviewed under the earlier `scoped` verdict, even when they push the range past 150 runtime lines or touch a gate path that would now make the depth full. Fix: on entry to a `scoped` pass, rerun `gstack-review-plan --range-base $RANGE_BASE` and fall back to the full pass if NEXT is no longer `scoped`.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The `"scope":"scoped"` marker is stripped silently. <reader>.md(.tmpl) and the CHANGELOG say a scoped pass logs `"scope":"scoped"`. But lib/review-evidence.ts:266 (bindReview, which runs on every `gstack-review-log --finish`) deletes any caller-supplied `scope` key, and only re-adds `scope:'fix-range'` for a start captured with `--fix-range`. So the marker never reaches the log, and scoped passes cannot be told apart from full passes. That breaks the stated plan to revisit the 150-line value "once classified findings carry raised_by", because the backtest data cannot separate the two arms. The receipt test writes `review_loop` by hand and never goes through gstack-review-log, so it cannot catch this. Fix: use an unreserved key (for example `pass_scope`), or let bindReview pass `scoped` through. Add a test that sends the row through `--finish`.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: Fix-check accounting in a scoped pass is ambiguous. The prose says a scoped pass's fix-check "is decision 3.5's reviewer and prompt … inside this pass". Decision 3.5 says to take a `review-fix-check` token and log a `review-fix-check` row. If the agent follows 3.5 literally, summarizeReviewLoop counts `fix_checks=1` after pass 2. A later at-cap blocker then plans another fix-check (nextStep never counts fix-checks), so the receipt shows two, against the "two full passes plus at most one fix-check" cap. If the agent logs it inside the review row, it never appears as a fix-check at all. Someone needs to decide which accounting is intended and enforce it in code.

label: FIXABLE
summary: Unsanitized text in FIX_RANGE can inject a line ahead of NEXT. bin/gstack-review-plan:134 interpolates `range.errors[].input` into the FIX_RANGE line. For binary_code_path that input is a raw repository path, and core.quotePath=false is set. A path containing a newline in the fix range would emit a forged line, such as a fake `NEXT:`, before the real REVIEW_PLAN and NEXT lines, and the skill says "its NEXT: alone picks the next decision". Exploiting it needs an attacker-named file inside the agent's own fix commits, so the risk is low. DEPTH_ERROR has the same exposure, but it prints after NEXT. Fix: run the input through the existing `sanitize`, or strip control characters before printing.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: raisedBy (lib/review-scope.ts:41) collapses any raiser outside the list, for example `codex`, `claude`, or a specialist label that does not normalize, to `unknown`, and that overwrites the finding's original `raised_by` in the classified output. That loses provenance for exactly the attribution data the 150-line revisit depends on. Consider keeping the raw value in a separate field when normalization fails.

Three of the --range-base fail-closed branches have no test: a base that is a real commit but not an ancestor of HEAD, an untracked-only working tree (collected.untracked.length), and a range that classifyDiff reports errors for. The CLI tests only cover an unknown sha and a tracked uncommitted edit. Each of these branches has to plan the full pass 2. If a regression reports runtime_lines for one of them, an unreviewed or rewritten range would quietly get the cheaper scoped pass.
fix: In test/review-plan-cli.test.ts, add three cases that assert FIX_RANGE: unread (<why>) and NEXT: full: (1) a range base on a sibling branch (not an ancestor), (2) a new untracked file after the fix commit, (3) a range whose classification fails closed.

summary: Conditional side effect in the scoped branch: the SKIP record for the specialist army ('specialists and <reader> (scoped pass)') sits in the else branch of the <reader> choice. When the <reader> is dispatched (Step 11 pending or numbers changed), the CLI prints no SKIP line for the specialists it left out, even though gstack-review-plan says it prints one SKIP per reviewer left out. And when --force specialists are dispatched, the line still says specialists were skipped.
fix: Record the specialist skip on its own, outside the <reader> branch. Name it 'specialists except forced (scoped pass)' when any are forced. Push an '<reader> (scoped pass)' skip only when neither <reader> dispatch is added.
test_stub: describe('scoped pass skips', () => { it('lists the skipped specialists even when the outside voice runs on changed numbers', () => { const plan = planReview(/* standard code diff, numbers changed, history { fullPasses: 1, last: 'full', fixedBlocking: true, rangeRuntimeLines: 24 } */); expect(plan.next.step).toBe('scoped'); expect(plan.dispatches.some(d => d.role === 'outside-voice')).toBe(true); expect(plan.skipped.some(s => s.startsWith('specialists'))).toBe(true); }); });

summary: The dispatch-compare replay never reaches the new scoped step. The 'blocker' outcome is { fixedBlocking: true } with no rangeRuntimeLines, so nextStep always returns full ('the fix range was not read'). That makes the scoped-to-full mapping added at line 89 dead code, and any cost or no-loss comparison this harness produces still prices the old full pass 2 with the specialist army. The CHANGELOG's claim that pass 2 now reviews the fix in proportion to its size is therefore not measured by the repo's own replay. The crew rule says review-depth changes merge only after a replay of the new policy.
fix: Give the blocker and fix-regression outcomes a rangeRuntimeLines (a fixture field, or one derived from RANGE_FRACTION times the fixture's runtime lines), add a case above SCOPED_RANGE_LINES, and assert that the blocker scenario dispatches fix-check, <reader> and adversarial on pass 2.

summary: The CLI classifies the fix range, then keeps only runtimeLines and drops range.class. So the documented rule 'a fix that touched a gate-class path keeps the full pass 2' depends entirely on the agent remembering to pass --touched-gate. The whole-diff depth covers most gate edits, because a gate change in the range normally stays in the net diff. It misses one case: the fix range deletes a test or code path the PR itself added. The net diff no longer shows that path, but classifyDiff marks the range as gate ('deletes N code or test path(s)'). The planner then picks a scoped pass, and when the range has 0 runtime lines and Step 11 already ran, it also skips the native adversarial pass. A test deleted to silence a blocker is the case where gate integrity matters most.
fix: When range.class === 'gate', set touchedGate (or record the range as unread) so the full pass 2 runs, and add a CLI test where the fix range deletes a test file that the branch added.

label: FIXABLE
summary: An empty fix range counts as a 0-line range and gets the smallest scoped pass. Where: bin/gstack-review-plan, the fixRange block (~L110-121), and lib/review-depth.ts nextStep plus the planReview 'scoped' branch. If --range-base resolves to HEAD itself, the checks still pass: HEAD is an ancestor of itself and the tree is clean. collectCommit then returns no paths, so classifyDiff gives class docs, runtimeLines 0 and no errors, and nextStep returns 'scoped' even though --fixed-blocking says a blocker was fixed. When Step 11's adversarial pass has already run, the plan sends only a fix-check and the <reader>, both against an empty `git diff $RANGE_BASE`. The pass is logged as a full pass, uses up the cap, and reviews nothing. A stale or recaptured PASS_HEAD triggers this, for example when decision 1 resumes after re-entry or the agent saves PASS_HEAD again after committing the fixes. The claim "I fixed a blocker" and "the range changed nothing" contradict each other, and the plan accepts both silently. Fix: when the range lists zero paths (or the resolved base equals HEAD), report it as unread ("empty fix range") so the plan falls back to full. A test-only fix still lists paths, so it stays scoped.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: Eligibility is measured once at the decision, but the range keeps growing before pass 2 reviews it. Where: ship/sections/<reader>.md L18 ("a repeat uses the plan run that picked it"), decision 3 (~L831-835), and lib/review-depth.ts nextStep. The range is counted and the depth is decided when the Step 9 decision runs. Decision 3 then runs the cut of fix growth, Step 5 and Steps 6-8 before pass 2 starts, and those edits land in RANGE_BASE..HEAD. Pass 2 still dispatches the scoped set from the stale plan. So a range measured at 140 lines that reaches several hundred, or later edits to a gate-class path, get only a fix-check, the <reader> and the adversarial pass, with no specialist army and no full-depth plan. A full pass 2 had the same staleness, but its larger reviewer set hid it; the scoped pass makes it matter. Suggested direction: at pass-2 entry, re-run gstack-review-plan with --range-base RANGE_BASE and the same flags, and switch to full if the range is no longer eligible.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: Nothing checks afterwards that a pass was eligible to be scoped. Where: lib/ship-receipt.ts parseReviewLoop (scope copied verbatim, ~L311) and lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts. A review row with "scope":"scoped" counts as a full pass toward the cap. The queue and the receipt only recompute and bind the depth. They never check that the recorded range had at most SCOPED_RANGE_LINES runtime lines, that the depth was below full, or that --touched-gate was false. --touched-gate and --fixed-blocking are flags the agent sets itself. So a mislabelled or mistaken scoped pass 2 on a large range binds at READY the same way a real full pass does. Deciding whether the queue should recompute the range lines at range_base..head and refuse a scoped row on an ineligible range needs a human call on the strictness of the trust model.

label: FIXABLE
summary: raised_by silently drops unrecognized reviewer names, which corrupts the attribution data meant to re-tune the 150-line figure. Where: lib/review-scope.ts raisedBy and scopeFindings (~L41-49, L171). scopeFindings always overwrites raised_by with raisedBy(finding). Any explicit value outside RAISERS (for example 'codex', 'claude-adversarial', '<reader> (codex)' or 'design-lite') becomes 'unknown', and the original value is lost from the classified output that Step 9 copies into the review log. docs/review-policy.md says the 150-line threshold will be revisited "once classified findings carry raised_by", so the attribution would undercount the <reader> and adversarial reviewers by exactly the names hosts actually emit. Fix: keep the raw value next to the normalized one (for example raised_by_raw), or add aliases for the known host names. This is not a gate defect and changes no verdict.

label: FIXABLE
summary: Ranges that span a base-branch merge measure and review main's changes. Where: bin/gstack-review-plan, the fixRange block (collectCommit(root, resolved, 'HEAD')). If main is merged into the branch between passes, RANGE_BASE..HEAD includes main's commits, and range.class is never consulted. Main's edits count toward the 150 lines, which mostly fails safe to a full pass. But a small main change to a gate-class path stays eligible for a scoped pass, and the scoped reviewers spend effort on main's code instead of the fix. Fix: count only first-parent branch changes (diff the range against the merge-base with the base branch), or treat any merge commit in the range as unread.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The skipped note is misleading when the <reader> runs. Where: lib/review-depth.ts, the planReview scoped branch. 'specialists and <reader> (scoped pass)' is pushed only in the else arm. When the <reader> runs, the plan records no SKIP line for the specialists it leaves out, so the plan output underreports what was skipped. Push the specialists' skip unconditionally.

label: Medium
summary: Gate-class fixes can silently receive the reduced review. `bin/gstack-review-plan:118–125` classifies the fix range, but preserves only `runtimeLines` and errors; it discards `range.class`. The subsequent plan uses the remaining branch diff's depth and the caller-supplied `--touched-gate` flag. If a blocking repair restores a credentials or gate file to its base contents, that path disappears from the branch diff even though the fix range changed it. The workflow only instructs the caller to set `--touched-gate` for an item 2.5 gate-scan path; that scanner lists test/CI/configuration hunks, not every credentials/runtime path recognized by `classifyDiff`. Consequently the automatic gate classification is lost and mandatory full specialist coverage can be skipped. A read-only reproduction classified a 20-line range deleting `lib/credentials.ts` and changing `src/app.ts` as `gate`, then obtained `next=scoped` with no specialists when the remaining candidate contained only `src/app.ts`. Preserve the range's gate classification and use it to prohibit scoped review, rather than relying solely on the net candidate and a manually supplied flag.

label: Medium
summary: The dispatch comparison never exercises the new scoped transition. `scripts/review-dispatch-compare.ts:75–90` never populates `History.rangeRuntimeLines`, and its fixture schema has no fix-range size. Every blocking-fix scenario therefore takes the explicit “fix range was not read” fallback and dispatches the old full second pass; the new `scoped` accounting branch is unreachable. This silently makes the comparison's advertised exact reviewer counts and estimated token savings describe a different policy from the one shipping. In a read-only reproduction with a 460-runtime-line standard diff and a 24-line blocking repair, `compare()` reported 19 new dispatches, while the actual planner produced 9 first-pass dispatches, 3 scoped-pass dispatches and 3 audits: 15 total. Capture or explicitly preregister fix-range inputs in the comparison fixtures and pass them into the history before using this output as evidence for the reduced-review policy.
